key_points.point: The document acknowledges that AI has driven record-setting productivity and nominal GDP growth, which are core accelerationist goals. It notes that AI agents operate without the limitations of human labor, such as sleep or health insurance, leading to massive margin expansion. From an accelerationist perspective, this confirms AI's role as a fundamental engine for economic prosperity. However, the document warns that this productivity is not translating into broad-based economic health, creating a tension between technological output and societal stability.
key_points.verbatim: Nominal GDP repeatedly printed mid-to-high single-digit annualized growth. Productivity was booming. Real output per hour rose at rates not seen since the 1950s, driven by AI agents that don’t sleep, take sick days, or require health insurance.

key_points.point: The document observes that the marginal cost of AI-driven tasks, such as coding, has collapsed toward the cost of electricity. This aligns with the accelerationist belief that market dynamics force the cost of intelligence toward zero. The document uses this to explain why incumbents are forced to adopt AI rapidly to survive. It acknowledges that while this commoditization is efficient, it creates a 'negative feedback loop' for human labor that the market does not naturally brake.
key_points.verbatim: But the marginal cost of an AI coding agent had collapsed to, essentially, the cost of electricity.

key_points.point: The document frames AI-driven automation as a massive positive supply shock that lowers costs and expands output. It notes that companies are redeploying savings from headcount reductions into AI tools to maintain output. From an accelerationist perspective, this is the intended mechanism for achieving post-scarcity. The document highlights the caveat that this 'rational' individual corporate behavior leads to a 'catastrophic' collective result for the consumer economy.
key_points.verbatim: Every dollar saved on headcount flowed into AI capability that made the next round of job cuts possible.

key_points.point: The document asserts that AI agents are now capable of performing complex research and development tasks that previously required weeks of human effort. It notes that these agents are 'substantially smarter than almost all humans at almost all things.' This supports the accelerationist belief in AI's superiority in complex problem-solving. The document acknowledges that this capability is what renders traditional human roles obsolete, creating a displacement spiral.
key_points.verbatim: They write essentially all code. The highest performing of them are substantially smarter than almost all humans at almost all things.

key_points.point: The document describes how AI agents have moved from simple tools to autonomous systems that perform continuous optimization for consumers. The document warns that this efficiency destroys the 'habitual intermediation' moats that previously supported the consumer economy.
key_points.verbatim: Commerce stopped being a series of discrete human decisions and became a continuous optimization process, running 24/7 on behalf of every connected consumer.

key_points.point: The document highlights how AI enables dynamic, real-time strategic planning and execution within organizations, replacing static human processes. It notes that companies are using AI to maintain output while reducing costs, which is a form of continuous learning and adaptation. From an accelerationist perspective, this is the ideal application of AI. The document acknowledges that this efficiency is precisely what causes the 'intelligence displacement spiral' by removing the need for human labor.
key_points.verbatim: The companies most threatened by AI became AI’s most aggressive adopters.

key_points.point: The document notes that AI capabilities have improved exponentially, steamrolling previous academic attempts to fit the data to a sigmoid curve. It acknowledges that this speed is outpacing the ability of institutions to adapt, creating a crisis of governance.
key_points.verbatim: The exponential steamrolled our conceptions of what was possible, even though every year Wharton professors tried to fit the data to a new sigmoid.

Excludes: Simple technological unemployment or cyclical recession models.
